scope_limits: The primary comparison uses the same executable, inputs, three independent proofs, queue, memory reservations and public-cache behavior. Only the location of template preparation differs. Both arms overlap native compilation with GPU work.
The primary measurement is total completion time. Per-proof latency includes waiting and overlaps other proofs; summing it would overstate elapsed time.
The three independent proofs cover the same twelve native graph leaves at offsets 4 through 15. They exercise the production preparation helper but do not constitute a three-transaction aggregate.
The earlier two-proof comparison against sequential r96 repetitions mixed scheduling effects. It is preserved as exploratory evidence and is not the matched optimization result.

The hierarchy and SHAKE request checks use r97, before the profiling-only control was added. Their older r95 references have identical workload scope but different source versions; each is a single sample.

No complete fresh N3/N4 workflow was timed. Native proofs are revalidated archives; transaction proof generation is excluded. Driver/kernel caches were not cleared, and one matched pair does not establish statistical confidence.

The previous full sixteen-leaf heterogeneous GPU validation and complete-tree soundness/zero-knowledge review remain pending. This scheduling pass neither changes the existing AIR constraints nor resolves those security-assurance gaps.

The first r98 worker attempt reached the 55-second process limit imposed by the remaining ledger allowance and its 30-second cleanup reserve. It was not accepted. The user approved a two-minute extension, and only that worker arm was repeated with a 90-second cap; the failed receipt remains preserved.
